title: Compliance Policy: Advance Beneficiary Notice of Noncoverage on Laboratory Test Orders
content:
## Who the notice is for

The Advance Beneficiary Notice of Noncoverage (ABN) is used on Laboratory Test Orders only for patients whose coverage on the order is Original Medicare Part B. It is never used for Medicare Advantage, Medicare Supplement, Medicaid, commercial or TRICARE coverage. The coverage named on the order, and its payer class on file, decide this.

## When a test fails Medicare screening

A test fails Medicare screening in either of two cases:

- **Frequency.** Its test number has a Medicare frequency limit for the class, and the same patient already has the same test charged, not credited, on another order that is not cancelled. That other order's collection date must fall inside the test's listed number of calendar days, counted back from this order's collection date (the collection date being day 0).
- **Medical necessity.** The diagnosis codes on the order do not support medical necessity under the applicable coverage determination.

**Frequency example (hypothetical dates, a test with a 90-day limit).** This order is collected on 1 July. Another order of the same patient, not cancelled, carries the same test uncredited and was collected on 15 April, 77 days earlier: the test fails screening. Had that collection been on 1 March, 122 days earlier, it would fall outside the window.

## Recording the notice

- An ABN may be recorded only while the order status is *information hold*.
- The ABN is signed by the patient personally, before collection.

## The patient's options

| Option signed | Effect on the order |
|---|---|
| Option 1 | The order stays billed to Medicare; the patient is liable if Medicare denies the test. |
| Option 2 | The order is switched to self-pay; Medicare is not billed and the patient pays the test's self-pay price. |
| Option 3 | The patient declines the test, which is credited with the reason *test not performed*. When every test on the order is declined, the patient cancels the order with the reason *ABN option 3 declined*. |

## Without a signed notice

Without a signed ABN the laboratory may not bill the patient for a Medicare denial of that test.
